refnamediv.refpurpose: Realtime scheduling policy service configuration files

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: These files configure the policy enforced by systemd-rtwatchd.service8, which hands out realtime scheduling and high priority to threads of unprivileged processes. See systemd.syntax7 for a general description of the syntax.
Each setting may also be specified via the corresponding command line option of systemd-rtwatchd, which takes precedence over the configuration files.

refsect1.title: Options
refsect1.para: All options are configured in the [RTWatch] section:

listitem.para: Selects the realtime scheduling policy to hand out. Takes either rr or fifo. Defaults to rr.
The realtime priority the service temporarily runs at while processing a request. Must be higher than the value of MaxRealtimePriority=. Defaults to 21.
The nice level the service runs at otherwise. Defaults to 1.
The maximum realtime priority handed out to clients. Defaults to 20.
The minimum nice level handed out to clients. Defaults to -15.

Clients must have set the hard limit of RLIMIT_RTTIME to a value no larger than this time span in order to be granted realtime scheduling. Takes a time span, parsed the same way as LimitRTTIME= in unit files (see systemd.exec5), i.e. without unit suffix it is interpreted in microseconds. Defaults to 200ms.
The maximum number of users, processes per user, and threads per user the service supervises at the same time. Requests beyond these limits are refused. Default to 2048, 15, and 25, respectively.

Configures request rate limiting: each user may issue at most the specified number of requests within the specified time window. The time window is specified in seconds, but other time units may be used with the usual suffixes, see systemd.time7. Defaults to 20s and 25.
Takes a boolean. Controls whether the canary based watchdog is enabled. Defaults to yes.

The interval in which the main loop signals the watchdog thread, and the time after which the watchdog thread takes action if it did not hear from the main loop. The latter must be larger than the former. Both are specified in seconds, but other time units may be used with the usual suffixes. Defaults to 5s and 10s.
How long to refuse further requests after the watchdog had to take action. Specified in seconds, but other time units may be used with the usual suffixes. Defaults to 5min.

Take booleans. When the watchdog takes action it normally only demotes threads the service handed out realtime scheduling or high priority to. If CanaryDemoteUnknown=yes is used all realtime threads of the system are demoted instead, except for those owned by root, unless CanaryDemoteRoot=yes is used too. The latter also applies to ResetAll(). Both default to no.
